assumptions:
1) Token accounting: TokenVolumePerDay is estimated from average tokens per request * daily QPS * 86_400s.
2) BaselineGPU_throughput_tokens_per_sec = 2.2M tokens/sec per A100-equivalent for mixed sequence lengths (our internal profiling).
3) ReservedGPU capacity billed monthly; autoscaling spins up cloud-on-demand GPUs at ~1.6x unit cost.
4) Cost model: Reserved A100-eq = $8k/mo, On-demand burst A100-eq = $12.8k/mo (1.6x). EstimatedMonthlyCostUSD = ReservedGPUs*8k + estimated_on_demand_hours*rate approximated by observed autoscale events. (Simplified for spreadsheet input).
5) ExpectedHeadroomPct defined as (Reserved capacity - steady-state demand)/Reserved capacity; target >=25% for SLA buffer.
6) Scenarios: FastDecay = higher churn after paid acquisition ends, SlowRebound = strong organic growth after initial ramp.
7) This sheet intentionally simplifies sequence-length variance — see linked artifact for per-workload sequence distribution histogram.
model_recommendations:
- Reserve commitment suggestion: staggered reserve starting at 6 GPUs month-0, increase to 8 GPUs months 1-3 if Base or SlowRebound observed; hold at 5-6 GPUs for FastDecay scenario.
- Autoscale buffer = 15-25% depending on scenario; use 25% for months with high marketing uncertainty (M0-M2).
- Cost levers: enable per-route KV prefix caching for top-10 heavy prompts, target 15-25% token savings.
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit for slow-rebound long-term candidate models; test per-model evals in Optimize pipeline to ensure <1.5% quality regression.
- Batching: adopt continuous-batching window 30-60ms for interactive routes to reduce GPU token cost by ~8-12% at expected QPS.
- Model fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to smaller model family when p95 latency > SLO for >10 minutes to avoid cascade.
- Contract phrasing: negotiate reserved pool flex that allows +/-2 GPU reassignments month-to-month for initial 6 months (minimize stranded capacity).
sensitivity_notes:
- Headroom vs cost: each GPU reserved increases fixed cost by ~$8k/mo but reduces on-demand episodes and per-token unit price. Breakeven analysis: if autoscale usage would exceed ~20% of capacity for >120 hours/mo, reserved capacity is cheaper.
- Demand elasticity: a 10% higher QPS increases monthly token volume proportionally but can push another GPU boundary once aggregate demand > BaselineGPU_throughput*ReservedGPUs.
- Latency risk: long-tail sequences (p99) consume disproportionate KV cache; add an alert when token/session length 95th percentile increases by >30% vs baseline.
- Scenario pivot triggers: set telemetry-based triggers (weekly rolling) for: 1) MAU change >15%, 2) QPS sustained > baseline+20% for 48h, 3) reserve utilization <50% for 7 days. When triggers fire, run quick reforecast and action playbook.
recommendation_summary: Short: Start with a conservative reserve of 6 GPUs at launch with a 25% autoscale buffer for M0-M2. If Base trajectory observed, increase to 8 GPUs months 1-3. If FastDecay triggers occur, reduce reserve to 4-5 and shift spend to on-demand; if SlowRebound observed, accelerate commitment to 10 GPUs and prioritize batching + caching. Primary goal: minimize months with >15% autoscale (on-demand) spend while keeping headroom >=25% to meet latency SLOs.
